question.text: What is the 'controlling ownership interest' threshold for identifying beneficial owners in a company under the IFSCA Guidelines?

answer.text: More than 10% of the shares or capital or profits
More than 25% of the shares or capital or profits
More than 15% of the shares or capital or profits
More than 5% of the shares or capital or profits

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the IFSCA Guidelines, 'Controlling ownership interest' for companies means ownership of or entitlement to more than 10% of the shares or capital or profits. 'Control' includes the right to appoint majority directors or control management/policy decisions. The Trap: The 10% threshold in IFSCA is LOWER than some domestic thresholds. This reflects the enhanced scrutiny required for international financial center operations. Don't confuse with the 25% threshold used in some other jurisdictions. Cross-Exam Context: In Series XXIV (domestic), the beneficial ownership threshold may differ. IFSCA-01's 10% for companies is stricter, reflecting IFSC's need for greater transparency in cross-border structures. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Different entity types have different BO thresholds in IFSCA: Companies = 10%, Partnerships = 10%, Unincorporated associations = 15%, Trusts = 10% interest. Remember these numbers!
